incidents.title: Apple Multiple Products: WebKit Pointer Authentication bypass (CVE-2024-27834) added to CISA KEV
incidents.summary: Apple iOS, iPadOS, macOS, Safari, tvOS and watchOS contained an improper authentication issue in WebKit that could let an attacker who already had arbitrary read and write capability bypass Pointer Authentication. Apple fixed it in Safari 17.5, iOS/iPadOS 17.5 and 16.7.8, macOS Sonoma 14.5, tvOS 17.5 and watchOS 10.5 (May 2024). CISA added CVE-2024-27834 to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Nov 4 2026 (due Nov 18 2026) based on evidence of active exploitation.

incidents.title: KeyDrift malware steals SD-WAN encryption keys from Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers hacked through CVE-2026-20127
incidents.product: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator
affectedVersions: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN releases earlier than 20.9 (migrate to a fixed release)
incidents.summary: Cisco Talos said on Oct 28 2026 that an APT it tracks as UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator that Cisco fixed in February, and installed a custom malware framework called KeyDrift. Its PolyFlame module is injected into the controller's vdaemon processes as an in-memory backdoor and relay, and its LittleFilch module hooks SSL_read to pull AES-256 key material for a preset list of edge routers out of decrypted control traffic, staging it encrypted for exfiltration. Talos calls the activity historical, says targets included space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology and policy research, and assesses with high confidence that the group's infrastructure overlaps with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train covert network. There is no workaround; upgrade to a fixed release and check controllers for compromise.

incidents.title: Cisco ASA and FTD zero-day CVE-2026-76418 exploited to crash SSL VPN firewalls
incidents.product: Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD)
affectedVersions: Cisco ASA Software before 9.16.4.104, 9.18.4.96, 9.20.4.50, 9.22.3.200, 9.23.1.48 and 9.24.1.27 (per train) with SSL remote access VPN enabled and secondary authentication on a tunnel group
Cisco FTD Software before 7.0.11, 7.2.13, 7.4.9, 7.6.7, 7.7.14, 10.0.3 and 10.1.1 (per train) with the same configuration
fixedVersions: Not affected: Cloud-delivered Firewall, cdFMC, Secure Access and Secure FMC Software
incidents.summary: Cisco patched CVE-2026-76418 (CVSS 8.6), a denial-of-service bug in the Remote Access SSL VPN service of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) software. Logic errors when secondary authentication is configured on a tunnel group let an unauthenticated, remote attacker send a crafted request while connecting to the SSL VPN and make the device reload; a successful VPN login is not needed. Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026 and strongly recommends upgrading. Devices are affected when webvpn is enabled on an interface and a tunnel group (including DefaultWEBVPNGroup) uses secondary-authentication-server-group. There is no workaround, but disabling secondary authentication mitigates it. Shadowserver tracks more than 51,000 internet-exposed ASA SSL VPN devices.

incidents.title: Foxit Workspace: SSRF in file upload and PDF export plus stored XSS in file share preview (CVE-2026-119431, CVE-2026-119433, CVE-2026-119432)
affectedVersions: Foxit Workspace (ai.foxit.com) before the Nov 6 2026 security update
fixedVersions: Foxit Workspace as updated Nov 6 2026 (no customer action required)
incidents.summary: On Nov 6 2026 Foxit updated its hosted Foxit Workspace service (https://ai.foxit.com/) for three Important issues. CVE-2026-119431 and CVE-2026-119433 are server-side request forgery flaws in the file-upload and PDF-export flows: insufficient validation of user-supplied URLs and network parameters could let an authenticated attacker make the service fetch arbitrary internal or external resources and return their contents (CVSS 3.0 7.7). CVE-2026-119432 is a stored cross-site scripting bug in file share preview: an attacker could upload a crafted file, share it, and when a victim opens or previews it the script runs in the application origin and may access locally stored credentials (CVSS 3.0 8.7). Foxit rates all three Important and says no customer action is required; the hosted service is already patched. Reported by mrfathoni.

incidents.title: LINE Armeria 1.43.0 fixes path-scoped decorator auth bypass, Thrift memory DoS, and SAML inflate bomb
affectedVersions: com.linecorp.armeria:armeria <= 1.42.0 (path decorator / CORS / FileService XSS ranges vary by advisory; treat all <=1.42.0 as needing 1.43.0)
com.linecorp.armeria:armeria-thrift / armeria-thrift0.9 / related Thrift artifacts prior to 1.43.0
incidents.summary: LINE's Armeria 1.43.0 security release patches three High issues published Nov 6 2026: GHSA-xqhm-4ph4-423v / CVE-2026-121823 lets attackers bypass path-scoped decorators (for example decoratorUnder("/admin", auth)) by inserting a '.' path segment that FileService, TomcatService and JettyService still resolve; GHSA-2pfv-5p52-crjm / CVE-2026-121824 lets a reachable Thrift endpoint allocate attacker-controlled heap from malformed TBinary/TCompact length fields before the body is verified; and GHSA-6hgp-j5h7-33m3 / CVE-2026-121820 lets an unauthenticated HTTP-Redirect SAMLRequest/SAMLResponse inflate into an unbounded buffer in armeria-saml before any signature check. The same release also fixes Moderate CORS any-origin route ignore (GHSA-386q-mrg6-jfj8 / CVE-2026-121821), Low FileService stored XSS (GHSA-x9vf-hjgg-cq25 / CVE-2026-121822), and Moderate armeria-xds symlink SDS confinement bypass (GHSA-m64h-m6r5-6jrx / CVE-2026-121819). Upgrade to 1.43.0.

incidents.title: Alpine Linux sshd password authentication bypass lets anyone log in to key-only accounts (CVE-2026-123158)
incidents.product: OpenSSH sshd on Alpine Linux (openssh-server, built without PAM)
affectedVersions: Alpine Linux 3.16 through 3.24 and edge: openssh-server (no PAM), or openssh-server-pam with UsePAM no, with PasswordAuthentication yes
Official Alpine tiny-cloud images 3.18.11 through 3.24.3 (alpine user with * password and passwordless doas) once any $6$ hash exists on the machine
incidents.summary: Alpine Linux warned that sshd built without PAM can be logged into without a password. On those builds sshd checks a password by running crypt() and comparing the result to the stored password field, borrowing another account's salt when the stored field has none. musl's crypt() returns "*" as an error when the password is longer than 256 bytes, and "*" is exactly what the stored field holds for accounts with no password, so the comparison matches. An attacker who can reach the SSH port and knows the name of such an account can log in with one connection by sending a 257 to 1024 byte password, as long as the machine has at least one other account with a $5$ or $6$ hash. Affected setups are Alpine's openssh-server package (or openssh-server-pam with UsePAM no) with PasswordAuthentication yes, on every release Alpine checked from 3.16 through 3.24 and edge. OpenSSH released 10.6p2 on Nov 5 2026 to avoid the bug in sshd, and Alpine shipped fixed packages for 3.16 to 3.24 and edge. The bug was assigned CVE-2026-123158 later the same day.

incidents.title: Keycloak SAML redirect-binding signature bypass lets attackers take over federated accounts (CVE-2026-117691)
incidents.product: Keycloak / Red Hat Build of Keycloak (keycloak-services)
affectedVersions: Red Hat Build of Keycloak (keycloak-services, rhbk/keycloak-rhel9) until Red Hat ships a fixed build
incidents.summary: Red Hat disclosed a flaw in Keycloak's SAML HTTP-Redirect binding (keycloak-services): the server accepts percent-encoded parameter names such as %53AMLResponse, while the signature check only looks at the literal parameter names. An unauthenticated attacker can use that mismatch to slip in a crafted, unsigned SAML message that Keycloak processes instead of the legitimately signed one, which leads to full takeover of federated user accounts. Red Hat rates it Important with a CVSS 3.1 score of 9.1 and lists the Red Hat Build of Keycloak as affected; Red Hat Single Sign-On 7 is not affected. Keycloak 26.8.2, released on Nov 5 2026, fixes it (the commit "Verify the SAML redirect binding message that is processed" closes CVE-2026-117691); Red Hat had not listed a fixed Red Hat Build of Keycloak release when the CVE was published. No exploitation has been reported.

incidents.title: TPC Software MatchPoint: static app credential, IDOR, and TLS bypass cluster (INCIBE-2026-841)
affectedVersions: MatchPoint platform / Android app versions prior to the latest release recommended by TPC Software (exact build numbers not published in INCIBE-2026-841)
fixedVersions: Server-side fixes for CVE-2026-111490 and CVE-2026-111493 already deployed by the vendor (apply regardless of app version)
Latest available MatchPoint app version for the remaining CVEs (per INCIBE)
incidents.summary: INCIBE-CERT coordinated disclosure of seven vulnerabilities in TPC Software's MatchPoint sports-facility management platform (INCIBE-2026-841, posted 2026-11-05). Three are critical: CVE-2026-111489 (CVSS v4 9.9) — a static credential embedded in the mobile app that returns an 'autorizado' token granting unauthenticated API access; CVE-2026-111490 (CVSS v4 9.9) — IDOR via the actingasuser HTTP header letting attackers reach personal, banking, and financial data, private messages, physical-access QR codes, and perform account takeover / balance transfers; CVE-2026-111494 (CVSS v4 9.1) — Android TrustManager accepts any TLS certificate and the app allows cleartext HTTP. Also high: local SQLi in the FCM push handler (CVE-2026-111492) and unauthenticated Images.ashx profile-photo enumeration (CVE-2026-111493). Medium: plaintext credentials in SQLite/SharedPreferences (CVE-2026-111491) and embedded APK config/keys (CVE-2026-111495). Vendor has already deployed server fixes for CVE-2026-111490 and CVE-2026-111493; INCIBE says install the latest app version for the rest. Reported by Sergi García Tárraga. No known exploitation stated in the advisory.
